articles.title: The True Story Behind Madden and the Video Game That Turbo-Charged the NFL
articles.summary: In 1984, Trip Hawkins, founder of video-game publisher Electronic Arts (EA), boarded an Amtrak train in Denver for a meeting that would one day prove monumental. He walked into the dining car to pitch John Madden, the CBS football commentator and omnipresent commercial spokesman who famously feared flying, on lending his name to a football video game Hawkins wanted to create. articles.title: America's Aging Air Travel Infrastructure Isn't Ready for Climate-Fuelled Extreme Weather
articles.summary: The U.S. is still reeling from a nationwide ground stop last Friday—the longest such flight stoppage in 25 years—which lasted more than four hours and resulted in more than 15,000 delayed or cancelled flights. And with Thanksgiving only a week away, the year’s busiest travel season is about to begin—bringing with it anxieties of further disruption . articles.title: Astronauts Just Finished a Year-Long Mars Habitat Simulation. Here's What It Was Like
articles.summary: If you’re planning to travel to Mars , remember to leave your emojis behind. Martian astronauts, like International Space Station (ISS) astronauts, will have unlimited access to email exchanges with their families at home—and in low-Earth orbit just 250 miles high where the ISS sits, those communications are virtually instantaneous. articles.title: The Democrats Who Voted Against Nominating Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker of the House
articles.summary: Representative Hakeem Jeffries of New York secured the vast majority of House Democrats’ support in his nomination for Speaker of the House . Eleven members of his party, however, voted against giving him the nod. The ballots were cast in secret, so the identities of some of the Democrats who cast “no” votes are not yet known. articles.title: 8 Things You Shouldn’t Say to Someone With Memory Problems
articles.summary: When someone develops memory problems , their loved ones often reach for the family photo album—and start quizzing them. Who’s that? Where were we? Come on, Mom, you know this one. Dr. Carolyn Fredericks hears about this approach from people who are new to caregiving and hoping to help.
